use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

claims.content: The use case is triggered when IFF/SIF surveillance data (Modes I, II, and III codes) becomes available to exchange, or when an IFF/SIF data management/reporting action is initiated via a J7.5 message (ACT = 0–3), or when data updating is initiated by an R² unit reporting No Data status for one or more modes or by an operator transmitting a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request.
IFF/SIF transponder data has been successfully exchanged in the applicable J-series messages (e.g., J3.1/J3.5 for surveillance data or J7.5 for management actions).
IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) has been transmitted in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages when available.
The C2 JU exchanges IFF/SIF transponder data (Modes I, II, and III codes) through the five IFF/SIF exchange functional areas, transmitting available codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The C2 JU exchanges IFF/SIF transponder data (Modes I, II, and III codes) through the five IFF/SIF exchange functional areas, transmitting available codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: One canonical instance: C2 JU has IFF/SIF surveillance data (Modes I, II, and III codes) available, transmits those codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages, and completes the exchange of that data without requiring a special-meaning-code J7.5 (ACT = 2) exchange.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The exchange begins when IFF/SIF surveillance data (Modes I, II, and III codes) is available to transmit in J3.1/J3.5 messages.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The available IFF/SIF transponder data has been transmitted in the applicable J-series messages; no downstream reporting or PPLI comparison is part of this goal.
in_scope_actions: Transmit available IFF/SIF Modes I, II, and III codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages
Use J7.5 (ACT = 2) to exchange codes that have special meaning for implementing JUs
Perform the applicable IFF/SIF exchange functional area: surveillance data reporting, unique Mode II code protection, clearing IFF/SIF data, IFF/SIF difference resolution, or IFF/SIF update request
excluded_adjacent_actions: Post-exchange reporting of locally derived IFF/SIF data after comparison with prior PPLI data
Downstream use cases that occur after the IFF/SIF data exchange is complete
variant_dimensions: Selectable IFF/SIF functional area being performed in a given exchange instance
Use of J3.1/J3.5 (PTI = 0) for available surveillance codes versus J7.5 (ACT = 2) for special-meaning codes

missing_aspects: Evidence supporting that J7.5 (ACT = 2) is used for exchanging codes with special meaning.

claims.content: When an IFF/SIF data conflict alert is received by the operator, the operator has the following manual actions at his disposal for attempting resolution of the difference: (1) update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message for any mode; (3) initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message for any mode; (4) change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of a Mode II code; (5) decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to the local data; (6) clear the operator alert for any mode. Until the conflict is resolved by manual means, the local ID data continues to be reported in the appropriate surveillance message with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 1.
If no valid code is currently held for the subject local or remote track/mode, a 'No Data' condition exists and is reported as zeroes in the applicable Mode Code field.

Data updating can occur spontaneously as a result of the R² unit reporting a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, J3.XC1. Receiving units which hold valid nonzero data will respond as required by the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix, Table 4.7-5.

For the J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report function, a receiving unit may report a difference in accordance with Table 4.7-5 when locally entered data changes from zero to nonzero or from one nonzero value to another nonzero value, or in response to a J3.XC1 'NO DATA' report on one or more mode/code while local nonzero IFF/SIF is held.

If the R² unit identifies that an ID conflict exists, the operator is alerted, the local ID data continues to be reported in the appropriate surveillance message with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 1, and the conflict is resolved by manual means.

For non-R² units, if a conflict is indicated, the unit inhibits transmission of the J7.0 (ACT = 1) message until the surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0.
A code of all zeroes (00 or 0000) is illegal for use as an assigned operational IFF/SIF Mode I, II, or III code.
Operators may be alerted when two or more tracks have the same Mode II code.

Diverges from the periodic reporting flow: instead of continuing to report, a JU with R² may initiate a J7.5 (ACT=0) message to clear one or more modes on the specified track, resulting in no IFF/SIF data being held on that track and causing the JU to stop transmitting the periodic J3 message containing the continuation word for that track.

Diverges from Step 2: upon receipt of a J7.5 (ACT=0) message, all JUs automatically set the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status, except that acceptance or rejection of a Mode IV Clear message may be automatic or by operator determination.

Diverges from Step 2: instead of reporting valid periodic data, the R² unit may report a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report (J3.XC1); receiving units that hold valid nonzero data respond as required by the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.

Diverges from Step 2: rather than relying solely on periodic automatic exchange, the C2 JU may, on operator action, transmit a J7.5 (ACT=2) IFF/SIF Update Request message to request updated transponder data from another unit; receiving units respond by transmitting their local data codes.
Diverges from Step 2: the C2 JU may transmit a J7.5 (ACT=3) Special Code message to exchange special-meaning IFF/SIF codes.

Diverges from Step 2: the C2 JU may transmit a J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report to report an IFF/SIF difference in accordance with the Difference Resolution Matrix; this report may be initiated by operator action at any time.
Diverges from Step 2: for Land (Ground) tracks where the J3.5C3 word is not implemented, only the J3.5I word Strength field is transmitted or received instead of the full J3.5C3/J3.5I field exchange.
The C2 JU with R² holds valid IFF/SIF surveillance data (Modes I, II, and III codes) for a track.
As the JU with R², the C2 JU is responsible for reporting the available IFF/SIF data in conjunction with periodic surveillance data.
The C2 JU transmits the available IFF/SIF Modes I, II, and III codes in J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages.
The C2 JU repeats the J3.1/J3.5 transmission periodically to report the valid data held for the track.
All other JUs without R² monitor the reported surveillance data and report different data by transmitting a J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message.

The C2 JU may also transmit J7.5 management messages: a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message to clear data when initiated by operator action, a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request with the applicable mode indicators set to request updated data from the R² JU, and a J7.5 (ACT = 3) Special Code message to exchange special-meaning IFF/SIF codes when special code data are held.
IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) is available to the system. Validity of codes for established tracks is determined as either 'Valid Data' or 'No Data'.

The C2 JU has the applicable IFF/SIF reporting role for the affected track: it is the R² unit responsible for standard IFF/SIF surveillance data reporting, or it is a non-R² unit that holds different IFF/SIF data and is responsible for reporting the difference via J7.5.
For a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request exchange, the initiating C2 JU has the applicable mode indicators set.
For a J7.5 (ACT = 3) Special Code Reporting exchange, the C2 JU holds the special code information to be transmitted.
C2 JU

quality_flags.detail: [goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal slot's scope contract is not aligned with main_flow. It claims that J7.5 (ACT=2) is used to exchange codes that have special meaning, while main_flow step 6 and alternative_flow step 5 identify J7.5 (ACT=3) as the Special Code message and J7.5 (ACT=2) as the IFF/SIF Update Request. The goal conflates these two distinct flows, so the goal itself needs correction/narrowing rather than adapting main_flow. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Source-level support for 'C2 JU' as the actor))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] Trigger allows the use case to start from any IFF/SIF data-management/reporting event, including a non-R² unit initiating a J7.5 (e.g., ACT=2 update request) or an R² unit reporting No Data. Main Flow step 1, however, unconditionally begins with 'the C2 JU with R² holds valid IFF/SIF surveillance data'. This does not continue from the non-R²/No Data trigger conditions and is directly contradictory to a No Data starting state. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (No cited card supports the track-specific scoping ('for a track'), the characterization of the data as 'valid', or that the R² C2 JU 'holds' the data as a precondition; these details were removed.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger explicitly lists multiple entry conditions: IFF/SIF data becomes available, a J7.5 management/reporting action is initiated, an R² unit reports No Data status, and an operator transmits a J7.5 (ACT=2) update request. Main Flow step 1, however, unconditionally starts with 'The C2 JU with R² holds valid IFF/SIF surveillance data', which only continues the data-available branch. It contradicts/restarts for the No Data and J7.5 management-action triggers, and those branches have no alternative first step before the optional management actions in step 6.

[goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal slot is over-broad and conflicts with main_flow. It packages all five IFF/SIF exchange functional areas into one goal, and its scope_contract/success scenario say J7.5 (ACT=2) is used to exchange special-meaning codes. Main_flow step 6 and alternative_flow claim 5 use ACT=3 for the Special Code message and ACT=2 for the Update Request; the goal's coverage_state also flags the ACT=2 special-code mapping as unsupported. This is a goal-side conflation rather than a main_flow gap.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger explicitly starts the use case for J7.5 ACT=0-3 management/reporting actions, including an R² No Data update and an operator-transmitted J7.5 (ACT=2) Update Request, and the Preconditions call out ACT=2 mode indicators and ACT=3 special-code data. The Main Flow, however, only continues the R² valid-data periodic J3.1/J3.5 path and the non-R² J7.5 (ACT=1) difference path; there is no continuation for ACT=0, ACT=2, or ACT=3 trigger events.

All alternative-flow claims anchor their divergence to 'Step 2 (transmission of available IFF/SIF data in J3.1/J3.5 (PTI=0))', but main_flow step 2 is the C2 JU's reporting responsibility, not the transmission step. The actual transmission is main_flow step 3, and periodic repetition is step 4; several alternatives ('instead of continuing to report valid data', 'rather than relying solely on periodic automatic exchange') logically attach to step 4, not step 2. The referenced divergence points are therefore mislabeled and not attached to the actual main-flow steps.

Exception flow claim 1 describes a conflict-alert branch and lists six operator manual actions, but it never specifies what happens after those actions: there is no return to a main-flow step, no termination/handoff, and no explicit terminal failure/prevention state. The branch ends with an action menu (e.g., 'update local data', 'clear the operator alert') rather than an exit condition.

The Main Flow ends with R² periodic J3.1/J3.5 (PTI=0) transmission and non-R² J7.5 (ACT=1) difference reporting. The Postconditions, however, require that locally derived IFF/SIF data has been compared with prior PPLI data and that the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator in J3 is set based on codes received in the J2 message. Neither PPLI comparison nor PPLI indicator computation is performed or reached in the Main Flow; the goal's success boundary explicitly excludes these downstream PPLI reporting actions.

Postcondition 0 requires that locally derived IFF/SIF data differing from previously reported PPLI message data has been reported. The Main Flow never performs a PPLI comparison or a PPLI-difference report; it only transmits J3.1/J3.5 and J7.5 messages. The goal scope also explicitly excludes PPLI comparison/reporting, so this postcondition is not reachable from the Main Flow.
